cv:
Maria Okafor — Senior Mechanical Design Engineer

Experience
- Senior Design Engineer, Velox Robotics (2019–present): Lead designer for gripper and end-effector assemblies. Built an internal CadQuery library of 40+ parametric components (brackets, flexures, gear housings) driven from a YAML spec, used by 12 engineers. Introduced GD&T on all production drawings and ran tolerance stack-ups for every new assembly.
- Design Engineer, Kessler Automation (2015–2019): Modeled sheet-metal and machined parts in SolidWorks; owned the design-table configurations for a 300-variant conveyor product line.

Skills: CadQuery, SolidWorks, FreeCAD, Python (pytest, numpy), GD&T (ASME Y14.5), tolerance analysis.

Writing: Authored the team's 'How to write a parametric part spec' guide; mentor junior engineers on design-intent documentation.
posting:
CAD Task Author (parametric modeling)
We are hiring CAD experts to write precise, verifiable parametric-modeling tasks. You should be fluent in CadQuery or similar code-first CAD, comfortable reasoning about constraints and dimensions, and able to document a task so another engineer can solve it.
reasoning:
cad (weight 0.4): Nine years of parametric CAD across SolidWorks and CadQuery, including owning design-table configurations for a 300-variant product line and building a 40+ component CadQuery library. That is exactly the code-first parametric depth the posting asks for, so 5. Evidence is concrete and specific, so confidence is high.

geo (0.3): GD&T on all production drawings plus tolerance stack-ups for every assembly shows they reason about constraints and dimensions precisely, not just draw shapes. Flexures and gear housings also demand geometric reasoning. Score 5.

code (0.2): A CadQuery library driven from YAML specs means they express CAD intent in Python and design for reuse. pytest and numpy suggest decent engineering hygiene. I stop at 4 rather than 5 because there is no evidence of software beyond this library (open source, larger codebases), and I should not infer more than the CV states.

comm (0.1): They wrote a 'How to write a parametric part spec' guide, which is almost the same job as writing a verifiable task for another engineer. Mentoring on design-intent documentation supports it. Score 4. The CV itself is clear, but I have no writing sample to judge precision directly.

Overall: a strong, well-evidenced match on every criterion. Confidence is high because each score rests on explicit statements, not inference.
